name: Mustang & Dolpo
tagline: Muktinath, the walled city of Lo and Phoksundo
meta_description: Mustang and Dolpo tours: Muktinath yatra by road, flight or helicopter, Upper Mustang treks to Lo Manthang, Tiji and Shey Phoksundo. Prices and permits.
summary: Mustang and Dolpo lie in the rain shadow north of the Himalaya. Most visitors come for Muktinath temple at 3,710 m, reached in a day by helicopter or 5–6 days by flight or road. Upper Mustang's walled capital Lo Manthang and Dolpo's Shey Phoksundo Lake need restricted area permits. Best months are March–May and September–November.
intro: North of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges, the Kali Gandaki river cuts one of the deepest gorges on earth and opens onto a high, dry plateau that looks more like Tibet than Nepal. This is Mustang. Its lower half, around Jomsom, Marpha and Kagbeni, is Thakali country of whitewashed villages and apple orchards. Above Kagbeni lies Upper Mustang, the former Kingdom of Lo, where red cliffs riddled with cave dwellings lead to the walled capital of Lo Manthang at about 3,840 m.

For Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims the region means one place: Muktinath at 3,710 m, where water pours from 108 spouts behind the temple of Vishnu and a natural gas flame burns at the Jwala Mai shrine. Indian families reach it in three ways. A helicopter from Pokhara takes 35–40 minutes each way and fits into one morning. A flight to Jomsom with two nights in the valley takes 5 nights from Kathmandu. A jeep over the Beni–Jomsom road takes 6 nights and costs the least.

Upper Mustang has been open to foreigners only since 1992, and its permit still keeps numbers low. Trekkers walk 10–12 days through Chhusang, Ghami and Tsarang, or ride a jeep to Lo Manthang in about 7 hours from Jomsom. In May the monks of Chode Gompa perform the three-day Tiji festival in the city square. Because Mustang gets very little monsoon rain, it is one of the few Nepal treks that works in June, July and August.

West of Mustang, Dolpo is wilder still. Flights from Nepalgunj land at Juphal, and a 7–9 day walk through Dunai and the Tarap valley crosses Numa La at 5,190 m and Baga La at 5,169 m to Shey Phoksundo Lake, Nepal's deepest lake, at 3,611 m. Lodges are few, so Dolpo treks use camping and simple homestays. Our packages here include permits, licensed guides, flights, jeeps and hotels, priced in INR and USD.

highlights.title: Muktinath temple at 3,710 m
highlights.text: Muktinath is one of the 108 Divya Desams of Vishnu and a Buddhist site called Chumig Gyatsa. Pilgrims bathe under the 108 Muktidhara spouts, dip in the two kunds and visit the Jwala Mai flame. It is reached by helicopter in a morning or by jeep from Jomsom in 1–1.5 hours.

highlights.title: Lo Manthang, the walled city of Lo
highlights.text: Founded in the late 14th century, Lo Manthang at about 3,840 m keeps its mud-brick wall, the four-storey royal palace and the Jampa and Thubchen monasteries, whose 15th-century murals were restored over two decades. It is reached by a 10–12 day trek, a 7-hour jeep ride from Jomsom or a 25–30 minute helicopter flight.

highlights.title: Tiji festival in May
highlights.text: Each May, Tiji fills Lo Manthang's main square for three days of masked dances by the monks of Chode Gompa, re-enacting the victory of Dorje Jono over a demon who brought drought. Dates follow the Tibetan calendar, 14–16 May in 2026, and lodges fill months ahead.

highlights.title: Kagbeni and the Shaligram stones
highlights.text: Kagbeni, at 2,810 m where the Jhong Khola meets the Kali Gandaki, is a maze of mud lanes around a red 15th-century gompa. Hindu families perform shraddha for ancestors on the riverbank, and the gravels yield Shaligram, black ammonite fossils worshipped as forms of Vishnu.

highlights.title: Cliffs and caves of Upper Mustang
highlights.text: Between Chhusang, Ghami and Tsarang the trail crosses eroded cliffs of red, ochre and grey, dotted with man-made caves cut up to 3,000 years ago. Ghami has one of the longest mani walls in Nepal, Ghar Gompa at Lo Gekar is linked to Guru Rinpoche and Tsarang keeps a ruined palace.

highlights.title: Shey Phoksundo Lake in Dolpo
highlights.text: Phoksundo Lake, at 3,611 m in Shey Phoksundo National Park, is Nepal's deepest lake, about 145 m, and turns deep turquoise in clear weather. Ringmo village and its Bon monastery sit on the shore above a waterfall of about 167 m. It is reached in 3–4 days' walk from Juphal.

getting_there: Most Mustang trips start in Pokhara. Tara Air and Summit Air fly Pokhara–Jomsom in about 20 minutes, only in the morning before the valley wind picks up, usually by 10 or 11 am. By road, the Beni–Jomsom highway runs about 160 km from Pokhara up the Kali Gandaki through Tatopani and Ghasa; a private jeep takes 7–9 hours, and buses take longer. From Jomsom, jeeps reach Muktinath in 1–1.5 hours and Lo Manthang in 6–8 hours on a dirt road. Helicopters fly Pokhara–Muktinath in 35–40 minutes and Kathmandu–Muktinath in about 1 hour 15 minutes with a refuelling stop. For Dolpo, fly Kathmandu–Nepalgunj in 1 hour, then Nepalgunj–Juphal in 35–45 minutes the next morning, and walk 2–3 hours to Dunai.
permits: Lower Mustang, including Jomsom, Kagbeni and Muktinath, needs only the Annapurna Conservation Area permit: NPR 3,000 for foreigners and NPR 1,000 for SAARC nationals, including Indians. North of Kagbeni, Upper Mustang needs a restricted area permit, which since November 2025 costs US$ 50 per person per day, replacing the old US$ 500 for 10 days. Lower Dolpo needs a restricted area permit of about US$ 20 per week plus the Shey Phoksundo National Park fee of NPR 3,000; Upper Dolpo costs US$ 500 for 10 days. Restricted area permits are issued only through registered agencies, with a licensed guide. Check current status before you travel.

months.weather: Jomsom −5 to 10 °C, Muktinath −10 to 5 °C, dry, clear, windy afternoons
months.summary: January is the coldest month, but the sky over Mustang is usually clear and dry. Muktinath helicopter yatras run most mornings, and the Jomsom flight and the jeep road stay open, though snow can close the road above Jomsom for a day or two after storms. Many lodges in Upper Mustang close and families move to Pokhara, so treks to Lo Manthang are not practical. Pilgrims who go now find Muktinath almost empty and the water of the 108 spouts icy.
months.tip: Take the earliest helicopter or flight slot in January, as wind in the Kali Gandaki grows strong by late morning.

months.weather: Jomsom −3 to 12 °C, Muktinath −8 to 7 °C, dry, occasional snowfall
months.summary: February stays cold, with occasional snow that whitens Muktinath and the hills around Kagbeni for a few days. Lower Mustang is quiet and pleasant at midday, and the Jomsom flight is usually reliable. It is a good month for a short Jomsom, Kagbeni and Marpha tour with Muktinath, if you pack warm layers. Upper Mustang remains largely shut, and Dolpo's high passes are snowbound. Losar, the Tibetan new year, falls in February or early March and is marked in the gompas of Kagbeni and Jomsom.
months.tip: Carry woollen socks and gloves for the bathing ritual at Muktinath, as the courtyard stays below freezing until mid-morning.

months.weather: Jomsom 1 to 15 °C, Lo Manthang −6 to 11 °C, dry, strong afternoon wind
months.summary: March opens the season. Days warm quickly, the apricot and apple trees of Marpha and Kagbeni flower late in the month and pilgrim traffic to Muktinath builds. Lodges in Upper Mustang reopen as families return, so the first treks and jeep tours to Lo Manthang start in mid to late March, still with frosty nights. Wind in the Kali Gandaki is strong every afternoon, so walking and driving are best before noon. Dolpo is still too cold for most trekkers.
months.tip: Bring a buff or scarf for the dust that the afternoon wind lifts from the riverbed between Jomsom and Kagbeni.

months.weather: Jomsom 5 to 18 °C, Lo Manthang −2 to 14 °C, dry, clear mornings
months.summary: April is one of the best months for every kind of Mustang trip. Muktinath yatras run smoothly, and the road and flights are at their most reliable. Upper Mustang is fully open, with clear views of Nilgiri and Annapurna from the trail near Chhusang and dry, mild days in Lo Manthang. Barley fields are being planted, and villages are busy. It is a good month for mountain biking from Muktinath down to Marpha, as long as you ride before the wind.
months.tip: Book April Jomsom flights early, because Indian school holidays and spring trekkers compete for the same seats.

months.weather: Jomsom 9 to 21 °C, Lo Manthang 2 to 18 °C, dry, warm days
months.summary: May is the warmest dry month and the month of Tiji, when Lo Manthang's square fills for three days of masked dances, 14–16 May in 2026. Treks and jeep tours to Upper Mustang are timed around it. Muktinath sees heavy Indian pilgrim traffic in school holidays. Damodar Kunda becomes accessible for helicopter pilgrimages, and late May opens the Dolpo season, with the passes to Shey Phoksundo Lake usually clear of snow.
months.tip: Reserve Tiji lodges in Lo Manthang at least four months ahead, as rooms sell out quickly for the festival.

months.weather: Jomsom 12 to 23 °C, Lo Manthang 7 to 21 °C, mostly dry, Pokhara rain
months.summary: June brings the monsoon to Pokhara and the lower Kali Gandaki, but Mustang beyond the Himalaya stays largely dry. Upper Mustang is green with barley and still good for trekking. The weak points are the approaches: Jomsom flights are cancelled more often by cloud, and landslides can block the road between Beni and Ghasa for hours or days. Lower Dolpo is good in June, with flowers around Shey Phoksundo Lake, but Juphal flights can be delayed.
months.tip: Allow two spare days in June for Jomsom or Juphal flight delays caused by monsoon cloud.

months.weather: Jomsom 14 to 23 °C, Lo Manthang 9 to 22 °C, light showers, Beni road wet
months.summary: July is the wettest month south of the mountains, yet Lo Manthang receives only light showers. Trekkers who want a summer trek in Nepal choose Upper Mustang or Lower Dolpo, accepting the travel risk at each end. Muktinath pilgrims should prefer the helicopter, which can use short clear windows, as the road below Jomsom is often blocked by landslides. The upper valleys are green and quiet, with few other visitors.
months.tip: Buy travel insurance with trip interruption cover for July, when road closures and cancelled flights are common.

months.weather: Jomsom 13 to 22 °C, Muktinath 6 to 17 °C, light rain, cloudy gorge
months.summary: August is similar to July, with rain on the approach and mostly dry days in Upper Mustang. Yartung, a horse-racing festival of the Loba and Thakali people, is held at Muktinath around the full moon of Janai Purnima, in August or September. Hindu pilgrims trek to Damodar Kunda for the same full moon. Barley turns gold across Upper Mustang late in the month. Jomsom flights remain irregular, so keep plans flexible.
months.tip: Combine a Yartung visit with Kagbeni and Marpha, but plan the return to Pokhara with a spare day.

months.weather: Jomsom 10 to 20 °C, Lo Manthang 3 to 18 °C, drying, clearer late
months.summary: September starts the main autumn season as the monsoon fades from the south. Upper Mustang's barley harvest is under way, and the light over the red cliffs of Ghami and Dhakmar is warm and clear. Dolpo is at its best, with stable weather on Numa La and Baga La. Muktinath traffic rises after Pitru Paksha, and families perform shraddha at Kagbeni during the fortnight. Late-month flights become far more reliable.
months.tip: Plan shraddha rites at Kagbeni during Pitru Paksha in September with a priest arranged in advance through your guide.

months.weather: Jomsom 5 to 18 °C, Lo Manthang −2 to 15 °C, dry, very clear
months.summary: October gives the clearest skies of the year and the busiest trails. Dashain and Tihar holidays bring Nepali and Indian pilgrims to Muktinath, so helicopters and Jomsom flights fill early. Upper Mustang is dry and cold at night, and the monasteries of Lo Manthang and Tsarang are open for visits. Lower Dolpo is still good in early October but cools sharply by the end of the month. Apple season in Marpha peaks, with stalls selling fruit, juice and brandy.
months.tip: Book Muktinath helicopters and Jomsom flights at least six weeks ahead for Dashain and Tihar dates in October.

months.weather: Jomsom 0 to 14 °C, Muktinath −6 to 9 °C, dry, cold nights
months.summary: November is dry, clear and quieter than October, with sharp views of Dhaulagiri and Nilgiri from Jomsom. Muktinath yatras are pleasant at midday but cold at dawn. Upper Mustang trekking is still possible in the first half of the month, though nights in Lo Manthang drop well below freezing and some lodges close by late November. Dolpo's passes may receive their first snow. Flights are usually reliable, with crisp mornings.
months.tip: Finish Upper Mustang treks by mid-November, when lodges start closing for the winter.

months.weather: Jomsom −3 to 11 °C, Muktinath −9 to 6 °C, dry, clear, icy mornings
months.summary: December is cold and clear. Many families from Upper Mustang move south for winter, so Lo Manthang is effectively closed to tourism. Lower Mustang remains open, and Muktinath helicopters fly most mornings, making December a good month for pilgrims who want quiet darshan without crowds. Road travel on the Beni–Jomsom highway can be icy above Kalopani, so private jeeps start late in the morning. Flights to Jomsom keep running in clear weather.
months.tip: Pack thermal layers for December in Jomsom, as hotel rooms are rarely heated beyond an electric blanket.

faqs.q: How to reach Muktinath from India?
faqs.a: Fly or drive to Kathmandu or Pokhara first. From Indian border crossings at Sunauli or Raxaul–Birgunj, Pokhara is 7–9 hours by road. From Pokhara, choose a 20-minute flight to Jomsom and a 1–1.5 hour jeep ride, a 7–9 hour jeep drive up the Kali Gandaki, or a 35–40 minute helicopter flight that lands near the temple.

faqs.q: What is the Muktinath yatra package cost from Kathmandu?
faqs.a: Our packages start from about ₹32,000 or US$ 390 by road in 6 nights, ₹54,000 or US$ 650 by flight in 5 nights, ₹52,000 or US$ 620 per seat for a helicopter from Pokhara and ₹89,000 or US$ 1,070 per seat from Kathmandu. Prices are per person on twin sharing, with hotels, transport and permits as described.

faqs.q: Is Muktinath safe for senior citizens?
faqs.a: Yes, for most healthy seniors. Muktinath is at 3,710 m, so walk slowly up the 15–20 minute path from the car park or take a pony. The helicopter option avoids any night at altitude. People with serious heart or lung disease, uncontrolled blood pressure or recent surgery should consult a doctor before travelling.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a permit for Muktinath?
faqs.a: Indians need no visa for Nepal, only a passport or voter ID. For Muktinath and Lower Mustang, Indian nationals need the Annapurna Conservation Area permit at the SAARC rate of NPR 1,000, which our packages include. No restricted area permit is needed below Kagbeni. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much is the Upper Mustang permit?
faqs.a: Since November 2025, as we understand it, foreigners pay US$ 50 per person per day inside the restricted area, replacing the old US$ 500 for 10 days. A typical trek spends 8–10 days inside. You also need the ACAP permit and a licensed guide through a registered agency, and solo trekkers can now apply. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can you drive to Lo Manthang?
faqs.a: Yes. A dirt road runs from Jomsom through Kagbeni, Chele and Ghami to Lo Manthang, about 6–8 hours by 4WD jeep. Our 10-day Upper Mustang jeep tour from Kathmandu starts from ₹1,13,000 or US$ 1,350. You still need the restricted area permit and a licensed guide, even when travelling by vehicle.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Upper Mustang?
faqs.a: March to November. April, May, September and October are ideal, with dry, clear weather and mild days. Because Upper Mustang lies in the rain shadow, June to August are also possible, though flights to Jomsom and the Pokhara road are less reliable. From December to February many lodges close and nights fall below −15 °C.

faqs.q: When is the Tiji festival in 2026?
faqs.a: Tiji is held over three days in the third Tibetan month, which falls on 14–16 May in 2026. The masked dances take place in the square in front of the royal palace in Lo Manthang. Our 15-day Tiji trek starts from ₹1,58,000 or US$ 1,890. Festival dates can shift, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Lower Dolpo trek?
faqs.a: It is strenuous. Our 16-day trek crosses Numa La at 5,190 m and Baga La at 5,169 m, with 6–8 hours of walking on several days and simple camps or homestays. Fitness and previous trekking above 4,000 m help. It starts from ₹2,25,000 or US$ 2,690, with Nepalgunj and Juphal flights, permits and a licensed guide.
